Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that is it from this short series and for the first time in a three-match T20I series, Bangladesh have got the better of Pakistan. Next up, Bangladesh have a bit of a break coming up as Pakistan travel to the West Indies pretty soon. We hope you enjoyed our coverage, but there's plenty of action to look forward to. Day 2 of the fourth Test between England and India is still underway and you can simply switch tabs and tune in to that game. Cheers!

There is hardly any time for any more chit-chat and Litton Das is quickly instructed to go on and collect the series-winners trophy and his team joins him under the umbrellas and they rejoice and pose for a team photograph.

Bangladesh skipper, Litton Das, scoots towards Shamim Chowdhury for a quick chat. Litton says that the boys played good cricket in the series and they just didn't bat well in this final game. Adds that they gave chances to a few players who didn't play in the first two games and want to build on it.

Jaker Ali is the PLAYER OF THE SERIES. Jaker comes up for a chat after collecting his award and says that it was a good series for them, even though they lost the final game. However, the interview is cut short as the rain starts to get heavier and heavier.

Sahibzada Farhan is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for his fine knock. Farhan says that he is happy because the team has won and he played the way he was told to. Adds that he had a chat with Saim Ayub and told him to leave it up to him in terms of the big shots.

Salman Agha, the captain of Pakistan, starts by saying he is very proud of the effort. He adds that ‘the never give up’ attitude was there on display and today the team had many contributions from different players. On Sahibzada Farhan's knock, he says it was heartening to see the way he played and also praises Saim Ayub for the opening partnership between both of them. He adds that Hasan Nawaz and Mohammad Nawaz also played good cameos. On the bowling effort, he says Salman Mirza has been a top performer throughout the series and he continued the consistent performance even today. He adds that Ahmed Daniyal also bowled well.
Time for the Presentation ceremony... but it will be done in a hurry as out of nowhere, the rain has started to come pouring down.

Earlier in the game, Litton Das won the toss and opted to bowl first on a deck that seemed to yet again have plenty in it for the bowlers early on. However, their bowlers were taken aback by Sahibzada Farhan's whirlwind of a knock as he hit the ball to all parts of the ground. Farhan notched up a half-century but in the middle overs, Bangladesh started to pick up wickets more consistently. There were a couple of standout cameos from Hasan Nawaz and Mohammad Nawaz that ensured Pakistan got to a big total. For the hosts, Nasum Ahmed was highly economical and got a couple of wickets as well and Mohammad Saifuddin bowled superbly up until his final over.

A disappointing end to what has been an incredible run of four straight wins in T20Is for Bangladesh, spanning across two series, both of which they have won, against their Asian rivals. As many as 5 changes were made to the side and with the likes of Parvez Hossain Emon and Tawhid Hridoy not in the lineup, the onus was on the likes of Tanzid Hasan and Mohammad Naim to deliver. However, the top order completely crumbled, and so did the middle order. However, the lower order had much more fight in them led by Mohammad Saifuddin who remained unbeaten on 35 but the hosts still lost by a big margin of 74 runs.

Pakistan had the runs on the board and just needed a half-decent Powerplay. Instead, Salman Mirza and Faheem Ashraf ran riot inside the first 5 overs and picked up as many as 5 wickets, with Mirza sealing a fine three-wicket haul. From then on, it was all about game management and Pakistan managed to pick up wickets at regular intervals. They did bowl a few front-foot No Balls and couldn't clean up the tail as quickly as they would have liked. A long way to go for this new-look Pakistan team but this win will do them a lot of good.
Pakistan end the series on a high and with a big win but Bangladesh still create history by winning the three-match T20I series 2-1 against a historically big team like Pakistan.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and around off, Naim punches it without much timing and in front of mid off before picking up an easy single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Salman Mirza to Mohammad Naim, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Classy shot! Fractionally short and wide, Mehidy Hasan Miraz stands tall and angles the bat face to punch it square and through the gap at covers for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Faheem Ashraf to Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Nice and full on off, Mehidy leans on and blocks it down into the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Faheem Ashraf to Mehidy Hasan Miraz, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Mehidy Hasan Miraz is the new batter in.

OUT! BOWLED'EM! Faheem Ashraf goes quick and full and straight, gets the ball to nip back in as well. Litton Das is tentative and hanging back as he looks to just clip it away but ends up playing all over the ball. The ball beats the gap between bat and pad to smash into middle stump, which goes carting off the ground and Bangladesh are two down inside 10 balls.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Faheem Ashraf to Litton Das, OUT! b Faheem Ashraf.

Commentary.Commentary: Good-length delivery outside off, Litton Das opens the bat face and steers it wide of the point region for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Faheem Ashraf to Litton Das, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: A bit slower and on a length outside off, eased away nicely but straight to covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Faheem Ashraf to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Oh, a high full toss around off, Mohammad Naim is completely taken aback and just jars at it. One hand comes off the handle and the ball gets skewed down the throat of the deep mid-wicket fielder. He takes the catch and the batters pick up a single. The replays do confirm that it was dipping.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Faheem Ashraf to Mohammad Naim, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a good length and around middle, tapped across through the square leg for a single. Faheem Ashraf has overstepped on his very first ball and a NO BALL is called. Free Hit upcoming...
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Faheem Ashraf to Litton Das, No ball!

Commentary.Commentary: Faheem Ashraf to operate from the other end.
Good length around the top of off, Das waits back and guides it down to deep third for a single. Just 5 runs and wicket off the first over of the chase.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Salman Mirza to Litton Das, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! SHOT! Good length on off, angling away, Litton Das prods forward and punches it sweetly through extra cover for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Salman Mirza to Litton Das, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Dug in short and over off, darting away as well, Litton Das pulls out of the shot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Salman Mirza to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nicely bowled! Pitched up on middle, it is the off-cutter that leaves the right-hander. Das looks to defend down the line but is beaten on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Salman Mirza to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Litton Das walks in at number 3.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Excellent review! Mirza goes a bit short and bowls it outside off, Tanzid Hasan gives the charge, looking to smash it through covers but seems to be beaten past the outside edge. There is half an appeal from the bowler but not from the keeper, Mohammad Haris for caught behind and it is turned down. Salman Agha has a chat with the bowler and takes the review. The third umpire checks UltraEdge and finds a clear nick and overturns the on-field decision to OUT.
Commentary.Howout: c Mohammad Haris b Salman Mirza
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Salman Mirza to Tanzid Hasan, OUT! c Mohammad Haris b Salman Mirza.

Commentary.Commentary: Starts over the wicket, pitching it up on off, a hint of away shape on that one. Tanzid Hasan flicks it nicely but straight towards mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Salman Mirza to Tanzid Hasan, No run.
